tagline.text: About 1 km of white sand on the Sulu Sea and the gateway to Danjugan Island

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱6,500–13,000 (room per night, breakfast included, high season)

children.text: Punta Bulata White Beach is a long white-sand beach on the Sulu Sea side of Cauayan, Negros Occidental. It sits close to the boat landing for the Danjugan Island sanctuary, so it pairs well with a Sipalay trip.

Punta Bulata is a point and bay on the Bulata–Elihan coast of the town of Cauayan, in the southwest of Negros Island just north of Sipalay. Maps list it as "Punta Bulata Bay" in Barangay Elihan, and the beach faces the open Sulu Sea. The beach is described as roughly 1 km of white sand, with clear, shallow water that is said to suit swimming and snorkeling.

The beach's main appeal is that it is a quiet stretch of coast with almost no commercial development. Most of it adjoins Punta Bulata Resort & Spa, so in practice it is a beach you enjoy while staying at the resort. The resort is reported to hold a Department of Tourism (DOT) AA accreditation, and with few rooms it rarely feels crowded. In exchange, there are almost no restaurants or shops nearby, so plan your food and supplies ahead.

One of the biggest reasons to come here is Danjugan Island. Off the village of Bulata, the island is a wildlife and marine sanctuary where a foundation protects lagoons, mangroves and coral reefs, and its boat landing is Antol Danjugan Port in Bulata. Punta Bulata is often described as a base for the island, about
20 minutes
away by boat. Island visits require an official reservation, so confirm that before building your schedule.
Getting here from Manila takes some effort. You fly to Bacolod and then ride a bus south along the coastal highway for about
3–4 hours

, and many reviews say the final stretch is rough. That distance is exactly why it suits travelers who want a quiet sea with few people. One more thing to know: some Google Maps listings mark "Punta Bulata White Beach & Spa" as permanently closed, while 2026 price tables and booking sites still list Punta Bulata Resort & Spa. Always confirm whether it is operating before you leave.
A long white-sand beach faces the Sulu Sea. The sand is bright and the water clear, so photos come out well, and the length of the beach means it rarely feels crowded.
The water off the beach is shallow and clear, and is said to be good for families and beginners. Ask the resort in advance whether snorkel gear is available and whether guidance is offered.
About
20 minutes

by boat, Danjugan Island is known for five lagoons, a bat cave, mangrove forest and coral reefs. Visits are by official reservation and come in several tour types, so book first once your dates are set.
The resort has a pool that looks out to the sea. It is a good place to spend time on days when the waves are high or the sea is not suitable for swimming.

Reviews mention a swing hung from a coconut tree at one end of the beach. A slow walk along the sand at dusk, watching the sun set over the Sulu Sea, is the most recommended way to spend the time here.

blocks.title: Kayaking, diving and other sea activities

children.text: The resort's information lists diving, snorkeling, canoeing, hiking and fishing as activities. Diving is often arranged through dive centers in Cauayan or Sipalay, so check before booking.
There is a spa at the resort, so you can relax with a massage. The remote setting and calm atmosphere are often cited as strengths.

items.title: 1-night beach relaxation
items.subtitle: Beach on arrival, Danjugan the next day

children.text: Check-in is usually from
. Drop your bags and go straight to the beach to check the water and the waves.
Swim and snorkel in the shallow water. Coral and fish vary with conditions at the beach, so keep expectations light rather than high.
Walk along the beach at dusk. It is a good time to watch the sun set toward the Sulu Sea.
Have dinner at the resort restaurant. Reviews say there is practically no other place to eat nearby, so check the menu and prices beforehand.
The next morning, after breakfast, head to Antol Danjugan Port in time for your Danjugan Island tour. Follow the time fixed when you reserved.
After returning from the island, check out and continue to Bacolod or Sipalay. Check-out is usually around noon, so ask to leave your luggage if you are running late.
Whether day visits are allowed, and whether any fee applies, could not be confirmed from official information. Contact the resort directly.
Leave Bacolod, reach Cauayan in the afternoon and relax at Punta Bulata beach.
Take the Danjugan Island tour in the morning, then relax on the beach or use the spa in the afternoon.
Head south to see the beaches and dive spots of Sipalay, then return to Bacolod or travel onward.
Cauayan and Sipalay are neighboring towns and the transfer is not difficult, but public transport is infrequent, so allow plenty of time.
A nonstop flight from Manila (MNL) to Bacolod–Silay Airport (BCD) takes about
1 hour 20 minutes
. Airlines and schedules change by season, so check before booking.
From the airport to Bacolod city you can take a taxi or shuttle. Some booking sites list a resort airport pickup (about
round trip per vehicle), but check whether it is still current.
Because the ride south along the coast is long, taking a morning flight and arriving the same day is the easiest plan.
One guide says to take a Ceres Liner bus from the Bacolod South Terminal toward Hinoba-an or Sipalay and ask to be dropped at Cartagena. The travel time is given as about
3–4 hours
in different sources.
From Cartagena or the highway, use a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) or a pickup arranged in advance. Reviews describe about
6 km
of rough road from the highway.
By private car or rental, the drive from Bacolod is described as about
2.5–4 hours
. Reviews say GPS directions led visitors astray, so follow the location the resort gives you.
Between Cauayan town and Punta Bulata you can use a tricycle or habal-habal. Fares depend on distance and negotiation, so ask in advance.
The boarding point for Danjugan Island tours is Antol Danjugan Port in Bulata. It is safest to leave the transfer to the resort or the tour operator.
Southwest Negros is closer to dry from November to May, which suits beach travel. Cauayan is hot all year, with average highs of about
and lows of about
, and roughly June to September is said to be the wettest period (Wikipedia annual averages).
Room rates also change with the season. Sipalay.com's price table effective October 1, 2026 treats November 1 to July 31 as high season and August 1 to October 31 as low season.

The closest lodging to the beach is Punta Bulata Resort & Spa. Booking sites describe a small resort of about 13 rooms (another site lists 22) with air conditioning, terraces, a pool, a spa, free breakfast and parking. Room counts and facilities differ by site, so confirm before booking. Rooms range from Superior rooms to beach cabanas, beach casitas and hillside casitas, and according to the price table effective October 2026 high-season rates run about
. Prices may change without notice.

Many reviews say the resort restaurant is practically the only place to eat, and that the food is average but somewhat pricey. It is easiest to bring snacks, water and any medicine you need from Bacolod or Cauayan town. Sipalay nearby has more beach lodging and restaurants, so on a stay of two nights or more it is worth eating or staying one day in Sipalay.
Before departing, confirm through the resort's official contact or a booking site that it is operating and has rooms. Some map listings mark it as permanently closed.
Danjugan Island tours are by official reservation, so book first once your date is set and arrange your stay around it.
Leaving Bacolod early in the morning lets you arrive before dark. Avoid driving the last rough stretch after nightfall.
Reviews say the road from the highway to the resort is rough, so pack light and, if possible, arrange a pickup in advance.
There are almost no shops nearby, so bring snacks, water, sunscreen, insect repellent and personal medicine.
It is safer to bring your own snorkel gear. Ask about rentals when you book.
Carry plenty of cash. ATMs and card payment may be limited around Cauayan.
If you bring children, note the reviews saying the long trip and the Danjugan tour can be tiring for small kids.

Punta Bulata White Beach mostly adjoins the resort, public access and day-use rules could not be confirmed, and some map listings mark the property as closed. Be sure to confirm its current status before you go.
When the sea is rough, avoid swimming and follow life-jacket and safety instructions.
There is no hospital or large store near the beach, so in an emergency you must travel to Cauayan town, Sipalay or Bacolod.
In the rainy season (June–October), Danjugan Island tours may be canceled or changed because of waves and weather.
Do not touch coral or marine life, and take your trash back with you. Danjugan Island is a sanctuary with its own rules.
Prices, opening hours and transport vary with the season and time, so check the latest notices.
A wildlife and marine sanctuary about
20 minutes
away by boat. It has lagoons, a bat cave and mangroves, and requires an official reservation.
A beach town just south of Cauayan with plenty of diving and beach lodging. It combines well with Punta Bulata in one itinerary.
A midway town on the overland route, with a market and basic services such as banks and ATMs. Around
January 25
it holds the Feast of the Conversion of St. Paul and the Lubay-lubay Festival. Schedules shift slightly each year, so check with the town hall.
The airport city and starting base. It is about
3–4 hours
away overland, and a good place to stay a night on the way back and see the city sights.
